\noindent\textbf{Correlating optical coherence tomography (OCT) with histopathology requires mapping every OCT pixel to the corresponding location on the H\&E section. We present a fully automatic, GPU-accelerated pipeline that removes background from both modalities, normalises H\&E staining, determines orientation (including mirroring) and scale without calibration of the histology scanner, and deformably registers H\&E onto the OCT pixel grid. Across <<NSAMPLES>> specimens (<<SAMPLELIST>>), the median target registration error measured on <<POOLN>> independently segmented lumen landmarks fell from <<POOLAFFMED>>\,\textmu m after affine alignment to <<POOLDEFMED>>\,\textmu m after deformable registration (90th percentile <<POOLDEFP90>>\,\textmu m; <<POOLDEFLT2>>\% of landmarks within one OCT pixel of 2\,\textmu m), with a tissue-mask Dice of <<DICEMIN>>--<<DICEMAX>> and OCT and H\&E tissue edges (including the epidermis) agreeing to a median of <<EDGEMED>>\,\textmu m.}
\vspace{10pt}
}]

\section{Main}
Optical coherence tomography (OCT)\cite{huang1991} images the surface of excised skin-cancer specimens without labels, but its interpretation rests on co-registered histopathology. Here, en-face OCT projections (mean of the five strongest depth slices of the tissue slab, in dB above the noise floor; \SI{2}{\micro\metre} pixels) are paired with 4$\times$ brightfield scans of the H\&E section cut from the same face. The two modalities differ in contrast mechanism (back-scattering versus absorption), in sampling depth (an approximately \SI{20}{\micro\metre} OCT slab versus a few-micrometre section) and in geometry: sectioning, floating and mounting stretch, compress, rotate and can mirror the section. Generic registration toolkits\cite{klein2010,borovec2020} require manual initialisation for such pairs and give no direct accuracy readout. We therefore built a dedicated pipeline (Fig.~\ref{fig:pipeline}) and an independent accuracy measure based on natural landmarks.

\section{Results}
\subsection{Preprocessing} H\&E background (glass, the cardboard holder, air bubbles, pen ink) was removed by combining optical density, saturation and hue criteria and keeping the single tissue section; Macenko stain normalisation\cite{macenko2009} mapped each slide to a common reference (Fig.~\ref{fig:pipeline}b). OCT background was detected by texture rather than intensity: background regions---noise floor, empty acquisition tiles and mounting medium---contain a high local fraction of near-noise pixels, whereas tissue does not. This was robust where intensity thresholding fails, for example when floating debris or a neighbouring tissue piece is brighter than the specimen. The shared $350\times350$-pixel tile pattern of the OCT mosaic was removed by an additive flat-field (Fig.~\ref{fig:pipeline}d).

\subsection{Registration} Orientation was found by a batched GPU search over 432 hypotheses (mirroring $\times$ 36 rotations $\times$ 6 scales) maximising tissue-mask overlap, after which the six best distinct hypotheses were re-ranked by image similarity using modality-independent neighbourhood descriptors (MIND)\cite{heinrich2012}. This disambiguates nearly round sections whose outlines alone do not determine rotation, and mirrored sections (mirrored samples: <<MIRRORED>>). A multi-scale affine fit followed by a five-level B-spline free-form deformation\cite{rueckert1999} (control spacing \SIrange{800}{50}{\micro\metre}, finest level on the native \SI{2}{\micro\metre} OCT grid) produced smooth, fold-free transformations (Table~\ref{tab:data}). The H\&E pixel size, unknown from the scanner file, was recovered from the fit (<<HEPX>>\,\textmu m per pixel). The non-rigid part of the transformation is small and smooth (Fig.~\ref{fig:deformation}): median displacements of <<DEFMEDS>>\,\textmu m, 99th percentile at most <<DEFP99MAX>>\,\textmu m, and at most <<DEFGT50>>\% of the tissue moving more than \SI{50}{\micro\metre}, at torn parts of the rim. Overlays (Fig.~\ref{fig:overview}) and full-resolution regions of interest with complementary checkerboards (Fig.~\ref{fig:rois}) show that follicles, vessels, clefts and the epidermal boundary coincide.

\subsection{Registration accuracy} Because no manual landmarks exist, we measured target registration error (TRE)\cite{fitzpatrick2001} on lumens: vessels, gaps and clefts are low-scattering in OCT and unstained in H\&E, so both modalities show them as near-zero intensity. Lumens were segmented independently in each modality and paired by unambiguous mutual nearest neighbour (within \SI{20}{\micro\metre}, similar area, distance-ratio test). Pooled over all specimens, <<POOLN>> landmark pairs gave a median TRE of <<POOLAFFMED>>\,\textmu m (90th percentile <<POOLAFFP90>>\,\textmu m; <<POOLAFFLT2>>\% $<$\SI{2}{\micro\metre}) after affine alignment and \textbf{<<POOLDEFMED>>\,\textmu m} (90th percentile <<POOLDEFP90>>\,\textmu m; <<POOLDEFLT2>>\% $<$\SI{2}{\micro\metre}, <<POOLDEFLT4>>\% $<$\SI{4}{\micro\metre}) after deformable registration (Fig.~\ref{fig:accuracy}, Table~\ref{tab:acc}). How landmarks are defined and the error is computed is shown on specimen <<LMSAMPLE>> in Fig.~\ref{fig:landmarks}: lumens are segmented separately in OCT (dark) and in the registered H\&E (unstained), each lumen is reduced to its centroid, centroids are paired only when the match is unambiguous, and the error of a pair is the distance between the two centroids (<<LMNTOT>> pairs for this specimen). A second, denser measure---the residual translation that would further align \SI{400}{\micro\metre} patches---had a median of <<RESDEFMED>>\,\textmu m after deformable registration, that is, about one OCT pixel. The landmark TRE is a conservative estimate: OCT integrates a thicker slab than the H\&E section, so lumen centroids genuinely differ between the two images, and residual mismatches in lumen-dense regions contribute a flat tail to the error distribution.

\section{Discussion}
The pipeline aligns H\&E to OCT with a median landmark error of about 1.5 OCT pixels (<<POOLDEFMED>>\,\textmu m) and a median patch residual of about one pixel, with no manual input, and exports both modalities and a common tissue mask in one physical frame together with complete provenance metadata. Accuracy was lowest for sample\_12 (Table~\ref{tab:acc}), whose OCT contains saturated acquisition tiles, whose pale H\&E yields few lumens, and whose lumens are dilated in the section relative to OCT; in its structure-rich regions lumen outlines nevertheless coincide. The epidermis lies at the tissue rim, so the OCT tissue mask must reach the true tissue edge: a mask derived only from the coarse texture map sat 70--110\,\textmu m inside the tissue, excluded the epidermis and pulled the H\&E rim inwards, which the edge-refinement step removes (OCT and registered H\&E tissue edges now agree to a median of <<EDGEMED>>\,\textmu m). Non-rigid displacements have a median of about 6\,\textmu m; displacements above \SI{50}{\micro\metre} affect about 1.5\% of the tissue and lie almost entirely at torn or frayed parts of the rim, and a \SI{700}{\micro\metre} pattern of 5--20\,\textmu m displacements in the interior corrects stitching offsets between OCT acquisition tiles. Otherwise, the remaining errors are concentrated where the section is torn or folded, at the cut edges of the OCT field of view, and in low-contrast dermis where neither modality offers distinctive structure. Three limitations should be noted. First, the landmark TRE mixes registration error with genuine anatomical differences between a thick optical slab and a thin physical section, so it overestimates the true error. Second, the H\&E pixel size is inferred rather than calibrated; if the scanner's calibration becomes available it can be fixed in the configuration. Third, specimen sample\_11 was excluded: its OCT field contains a second tissue piece and mounting medium in contact with the section, and it was set aside for separate handling.

\section{Methods}
\subsection{Data} Each specimen comprises a 4$\times$ H\&E RGB(A) TIFF without physical calibration and an OCT en-face \texttt{recon\_xy\_topk} TIFF (float32, dB above the depth-dependent noise floor, NaN outside the reconstructed footprint, \SI{2}{\micro\metre} pixels; 0.7\,mm acquisition patches of $350\times350$ pixels).

\subsection{H\&E preprocessing} The glass brightness $I_0$ was estimated per channel as the median of bright, unsaturated pixels. Optical density $\mathrm{OD}=-\ln(I/I_0)$ was computed at 1/8 resolution; tissue was defined as $\sum\mathrm{OD}>0.12$, HSV saturation $>0.10$ and hue outside the tan (holder) and blue (ink) ranges, followed by opening, closing (radius 48 full-resolution pixels), retention of components $\ge$25\% of the largest, and hole filling. Macenko normalisation\cite{macenko2009} estimated the stain matrix from up to $10^6$ tissue pixels (OD $>0.15$ in all channels, 1st/99th angle percentiles) and mapped concentrations to the standard reference (H $=[0.5626,0.7201,0.4062]$, E $=[0.2159,0.8012,0.5581]$, maximum concentrations 1.9705 and 1.0308). Background was set to white.

\subsection{OCT preprocessing} The local fraction of near-noise pixels, $f=G_{\sigma}\ast[\,v<4\,\mathrm{dB}\ \vee\ v=\mathrm{NaN}\,]$ with $\sigma=\SI{160}{\micro\metre}$, was thresholded ($f<0.35$) at 1/4 resolution. After a \SI{20}{\micro\metre} opening, retention of large components and hole filling, debris attached by bridges narrower than about \SI{480}{\micro\metre} was cut by an opening followed by a nearest-component (Voronoi) assignment, and touching lobes were split by a distance-transform watershed\cite{beucher1993} when their neck was narrower than 0.6 times the smaller lobe's inscribed radius. The tile flat-field was the Gaussian-smoothed median over fully-tissue tiles of (tile $-$ tile median), subtracted in dB. Because the \SI{160}{\micro\metre} texture scale places the mask edge 50--110\,\textmu m inside the tissue, which would exclude the epidermis, the edge was then refined: a fine-scale tissue map ($\sigma=\SI{8}{\micro\metre}$, $f<0.5$, \SI{10}{\micro\metre} opening to cut bridges to fragments) was added wherever it lay within \SI{200}{\micro\metre} of the coarse mask and was connected to it, bringing the median distance between the reconstruction footprint edge and the mask edge to 5--38\,\textmu m. Intensities were clipped to the 0.5th--99.5th percentiles inside the mask and scaled to $[0,1]$.

\subsection{Transformation model} Let $\mathbf{x}$ be OCT coordinates in micrometres. The H\&E pixel position is $\mathbf{p}=\mathbf{A}_0\big[(\mathbf{I}+\mathbf{M})(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{c})+\mathbf{c}+\mathbf{d}\big]+\mathbf{t}_0$, where $\mathbf{A}_0,\mathbf{t}_0$ encode the initial similarity transform (scale, rotation, optional mirroring), $\mathbf{M},\mathbf{d}$ the affine refinement about the image centre $\mathbf{c}$, and $\mathbf{u}=\sum_\ell \mathcal{B}(\mathbf{C}_\ell)$ a sum of cubically interpolated control grids $\mathbf{C}_\ell$. Images were sampled with bilinear (optimisation) or bicubic (export) interpolation in PyTorch\cite{paszke2019} on an NVIDIA A40.

\subsection{Similarity} The moving image was the summed optical density of the normalised H\&E, so lumens and background are near zero in both modalities. The loss was $\mathcal{L}=\overline{w\,\|\mathrm{MIND}(F)-\mathrm{MIND}(M\circ T)\|^2}+0.5\,(1-\mathrm{Dice})$, with 8-neighbourhood MIND\cite{heinrich2012} (Gaussian radius 2 and dilation 2 pixels for initialisation and affine fitting; radius 1 and dilation 1 for deformation), a weight $w$ covering both tissue masks, and soft mask Dice.

\subsection{Optimisation} (i) Initialisation: 432 hypotheses (mirroring $\{\pm1\}$ $\times$ rotations \ang{-180}--\ang{170} in \ang{10} steps $\times$ 6 log-spaced pixel sizes from 1.3 to 2.3\,\textmu m) were optimised jointly (rotation, scale, translation; Adam, 200 iterations) for soft mask Dice at \SI{32}{\micro\metre}; the six best distinct hypotheses (differing in mirroring or by more than \ang{20}) were refined for 100 affine iterations and ranked by $\mathcal{L}$. (ii) Affine: \SI{32}{}, \SI{16}{} and \SI{8}{\micro\metre} levels (300/200/150 iterations). (iii) Mask refinement: the OCT mask was intersected with the affine-registered H\&E mask dilated by \SI{100}{\micro\metre}, and the affine fit was repeated if more than 0.5\% was removed. (iv) Deformation: levels at \SI{16}{}, \SI{8}{}, \SI{4}{}, \SI{2}{} and \SI{2}{\micro\metre} with control spacing \SI{800}{}, \SI{400}{}, \SI{200}{}, \SI{100}{} and \SI{50}{\micro\metre} (450/400/300/250/250 iterations); each level adds a new control grid while earlier grids stay fixed, and the regulariser is $\lambda_\ell\overline{\|\nabla\mathbf{u}\|^2}+10\,\overline{\max(0,0.1-\det J)}$ with $\lambda_\ell=1,0.5,0.25,0.1,0.05$. These settings were chosen in a sweep on 12umA scored by landmark TRE.

\subsection{Accuracy assessment} Lumens were segmented as $G_{1}\ast I<0.1$ within the tissue mask eroded by \SI{80}{\micro\metre}, with areas of \SIrange{60}{12000}{\square\micro\metre}; pairs were mutual nearest neighbours within \SI{20}{\micro\metre} with area ratio $>0.3$ that were unambiguous in both directions (nearest/second-nearest distance ratio $<0.5$, after Lowe), which rejects chance pairings in lumen-dense tissue. Block matching computed, for \SI{400}{\micro\metre} patches (50\% overlap) at \SI{4}{\micro\metre} resolution, the integer shift within $\pm$\SI{40}{\micro\metre} that minimised the MIND sum of squared differences, refined to sub-pixel precision by a parabolic fit; patches with $<$90\% tissue, indistinct minima or minima on the search border were excluded. Because block matching uses the optimised similarity measure, it is reported as a consistency check, whereas the landmark TRE is independent of the optimiser.

\subsection{Outputs} For each specimen, \texttt{output/} contains lossless TIFFs on (i) the native OCT grid (\SI{2}{\micro\metre}) and (ii) an H\&E-native grid over the same physical frame: OCT (dB), registered H\&E (normalised and original colours), and OCT, H\&E and common tissue masks (common mask $=$ OCT $\wedge$ registered H\&E). Every TIFF is ImageJ-calibrated and embeds the complete metadata, which is also written to a single \texttt{<sample>\_metadata.json}: inputs with SHA-256 checksums, pixel sizes, coordinate frame and its conversion to OCT scanner millimetres, transform parameters, preprocessing parameters, stain matrices, accuracy metrics and software versions. The full transform (\texttt{transform\_full.npz}) and a dense per-pixel map are kept for mapping annotations in either direction.

\subsection{Quality control of the epidermis} Because the epidermis lies at the tissue rim, a per-specimen figure (\texttt{scripts/epidermis\_check.py}) shows six \SI{800}{\micro\metre} edge regions with the OCT, registered H\&E and common-mask outlines and both images restricted to the common mask; in all four specimens the epidermis and stratum corneum lie inside all three masks, and the OCT/H\&E tissue-edge distance is reported per specimen (Table~\ref{tab:acc}).

\subsection{Software} Registration runs on NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA), Apple-silicon GPUs (Metal/MPS) or the CPU. The B-spline displacement on the regular sampling grid is evaluated as two matrix products with exact bicubic weights ($\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{W}_y\mathbf{C}\mathbf{W}_x^\top$), identical to bicubic grid sampling to within \SI{e-4}{\micro\metre} and an order of magnitude faster on CPUs. Runtimes in Table~\ref{tab:data} are for an NVIDIA A40; without an NVIDIA GPU a standard run takes about an hour or more per specimen.

\subsection{Code and data availability} {\raggedright Code: \url{https://github.com/atesfet/heoct-registration-studio-v1} (Registration Studio v1: pipeline, interactive web viewer, launchers for Linux, macOS and Windows; conda environment \texttt{reg\_env}); local copy \texttt{/home/adlz/atesfet/dev/registration/v1}. Registered data, one folder per specimen with stages \texttt{01}--\texttt{06} and the final \texttt{output/} folder: \texttt{/home/adlz/atesfet/dev/data\_12um\_registered/<sample>/}. This report and the cross-specimen figures: \texttt{/home/adlz/atesfet/dev/registration/v1/\{report,figures\}/}.\par}
